domain-warp-curl.look: Single octave at matched mean displacement (0.71 features): curl of a Perlin potential and the independent-per-axis warp (DomainWarpGradient style) look nearly the same on bands and on Worley; only the gradient-of-potential warp is clearly different (bands pinch into bubbles, cells crumple into ridge networks). With 3 progressive octaves the difference becomes obvious: curl gives marbling with even filament density everywhere, the independent warp gives tight folds next to large dilated smooth patches, the gradient warp crumples into bubble-wrap domains. SparseVortex potential (3x3 window, first-order tangent push) makes concentric ring eyes in the bands at A=2; with Density 0.3-0.4 eyes sit in calm band regions, which reads as a cartoon Jupiter. Eyes are target-like rings rather than spirals because the push is tangential, not a rotation. 3D (grad phi x grad psi) works: XZ slice shows eyes and swirls, isosurface is a dense swirled blob field.

domain-warp-curl.port_notes: Warp() family. Perlin potential needs value+gradient from one lattice visit (perlin2h / perlin3g). Scalar: oct1 147 ns, oct3 310 ns, SparseVortex 184 ns (3.7x), independent reference 219 ns (4.4x), so curl is cheaper than the existing-style warp here. Density gate must be smooth: 1 - smoothstep(dens, dens+.15, rnd).

critic.notes: Ship, but not the node reported. Keep the analytic potential, add a Steps int (default 4) and a Mode {Curl, Gradient}, remove the sparse kernels. A single step does not earn a node: on bands it is hard to pick from the independent warp, and at matched displacement 0.43 its det J spread is 2.07 with 28% folded pixels against 1.45 and 24% for real DomainWarpSimplex, so one Euler step is not area preserving in practice. On Worley it does differ: cells stay even and worm-like where real Simplex and SuperSimplex keep large dilated cushions and star junctions. With 4 sub-steps it becomes the clean hooks and eyes the report credits to 8-16 steps of DomainWarpFlow: steps 4 and 12 look nearly the same on bands and Worley. A technical artist would reach for this for marble, agate, ink and smoke. The matching FD graph is 45 nodes. Real shear stacks are a cheaper rival for even marble (6 pairs rotated: 43 nodes, 16.01 / 33.34 / 55.73 ns) but give zigzags with no hooks. Not a terrain warp: fBm relief through it is streaked long folds, and real Simplex streaks too.
critic.improved: Added steps to t_domain_warp_curl.cpp (additive; previous copy t_domain_warp_curl.prev2.cpp). Helped decisively: marbling at far lower cost than assumed, plus plates from the same loop. Real-node FD stir on other potentials at matched displacement: Simplex FS96 gives sharp varied hooks with no T motif and SuperSimplex FS96 softer flowing ones, both arguably better looking than Perlin. Antisymmetric simplex kernels as stir velocity: rejected, regular pinwheel lattice.

tournament.notes: Ship with a Steps int and Mode {Curl, Gradient}, without sparse kernels. One step does not earn a node on bands, though it does keep cells even on Worley. Four steps match 12 by eye: clean hooks and eyes. The matching FD graph is 45 nodes at 24.96 / 44.78 / 72.08 ns AVX2 and passes fnlab check clean. Analytic port is estimated at about 6-8 ns 2D, unmeasured. Reported c0 reproduced (6.33 against 5.8 at oct3); steps=4 reads c0 7.44 on seed 2024 and 7.30 on seed 555, while 3 octaves with steps falls to c0 1.00 with hair grain. Perlin lattice shows as T and mushroom motifs and a ray star in the FFT. Real Simplex FS96 and SuperSimplex FS96 potentials looked better in 2D, but warn on continuity in 3D/4D and 4D. Not a terrain warp.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: estimate: ~2 / 4 / 8 ns per warp octave (Perlin with gradient, 3D two potentials); SparseVortex 3^d ~3 / 10 / 33 ns

artist-terrain.note: Even-filament marbling, keeps Worley cells equal size; 4 sub-steps give hooks and eyes. Analytic ~6-8 ns estimate, unported. Planet cloud bands and gas giants.

artist-material.note: Clean hooks and eyes at low step counts. This is the marble and smoke tool I would use daily.

voxel-engineer.note: Four-step curl is clean hooks without pinches: 0% folded at 4 steps by critic's count. Est 6-8 ns 2D unported. Vol is messy but better than a bare warp.

maintainer.note: Divergence-free warp with Steps: 4 steps give clean hooks and eyes, folded pixels 28.6 to 0 percent from 1 to 4 steps. ~2/4/8 ns per octave est, fits the DomainWarp family with one int and one 2-value enum. Exactly the shape of node I want.

graphics-researcher.note: Curl noise is Bridson; the useful finding is sub-stepping (4 Euler steps remove folds, det J spread 2.13 to 0.59) and Gradient mode plates. Ship, but it is a known kernel.

creative.note: Hard ink swirls with hooks. Strong in black and white.

plan_node.range: Warp: output is the Source's, Path Average is a weighted mean of Source samples. No ScaleOutput. The measured constants are the speed scales instead, 0.7485 / 0.858 / 0.942 and 0.912 for the 3D cross, so Warp Amplitude is the rms path length on Perlin (measured 0.99 to 1.02 over 3 seeds in every dimension), peak 2.3 x in 2D and 4D, 4.8 x in 3D Curl.
notes: Prototype amplitudes map as Warp Amplitude = 0.75 x A x Feature Scale, the prototype rms speed is 0.75 (mean displacement 0.693 against 0.92 here). L in the flow prototype maps to 1.6 x L x Feature Scale. Gradient mode descends at positive amplitude, so A=-3.33 is 2.5 x Feature Scale.

master.one_liner: Divergence-free warp family: swirling folds with no pinches or bubbles, with a Potential enum covering lattice curl noise, sparse vortices, and curl of any source.
master.look: Prototype cl_vortex: curl warp of stripes folds and streaks like marble with even line density; gradient warp of the same source pinches into bubble rings. SparseVortex at A=2-4 winds stripes into agate eyes and Jupiter eddies, separated by calm zones when Density <1. Marbling, smoke, gas giants, rivers that avoid a mask.
master.algorithm:
v=A*grad(psi) with A antisymmetric, so div v=0 because the Hessian is symmetric.
2D: v=(d_y psi,-d_x psi).
3D: v=grad(phi) x grad(psi) from two potentials sharing lattice corners (cheaper than Bridson's 3 potential curl).
4D: single potential v=(d_y,-d_x,d_w,-d_z)psi, which keeps GenTileable2D working.
Potential enum:
- Simplex: analytic gradient from the simplex corners.
- SparseVortex: window of jittered sites, v=sum_i G_i*A_i*d_i*s(r_i), s=(1-r^2/R^2)^3. A_i=J in 2D, cross with hash axis in 3D, hash-chosen skew plane in 4D. This is exactly divergence free since d^T A d=0 and tr A=0. Site kept when rnd<Density; G from hash with sign.
- Source: any generator via tetrahedral FD.
Constraint (Bridson boundary): psi'=psi*ramp(g(x)), so v=ramp*A*grad psi+psi*ramp'*A*grad g, tangent to g=0 contours, via FD on g. Warp() adds amp*v to the positions, so the Fractal warp nodes work unchanged.
master.why_new: Existing warps use independent vector noise, so they are compressible and pinch. Curl warp preserves area to first order, so thresholded area of a mask stays stable. Constraint-aware flow and localized eddies are impossible with a plain Warp Amplitude hybrid because scaling the velocity by a mask breaks the divergence-free property.
master.simd_plan:
Simplex: ~1.2x simplex with gradient, about 2/3.5/5 ns (3D shares hash fields for 2 gradient sets; 4D single potential). SparseVortex 3^d: polys only, no sqrt, no trig, ~.8x Cellular cost = ~3/10/33 ns; R<=1.2 with jitter +-.3 is seam free. Optional 2^d window with lower jitter and R<=.9: 4/8/16 sites for ~1.8/3.6/8 ns. Source: (d+1) x Source per Warp. Fixed count all modes; plugs into the existing Warp virtual functions.
[DomainWarpCurl, volumetric-3d4d] DomainWarpSimplex.inl pattern, Perlin lattice; value+gradient per potential ~2x Perlin FMAs; 3D with 3 potentials ~3x Perlin 3D (~7 ns per warp), 2D ~2x Perlin 2D, 4D 6 potentials ~4x Perlin 4D (~17 ns). Branch-free.
master.continuity: C1 for Simplex potential at least (source of warp C2+), c0ratio 7.99 in the vortex prototype. No seams when R fits the window.
master.params: Enum: Potential. Hybrid: Warp Amplitude, Density, Constraint source. Float: Vortex Radius R. Standard DomainWarp frequency, axis scale and seed offset.
master.risks:
Divergence-free holds for the velocity, not the finite displacement: large amplitude still folds, so a multi-step option or the Progressive fractal may be needed. 3D form is not a true curl of one vector potential, but is still solenoidal. Tangent-only flow does not enforce no-slip. Only 2D was prototyped.
[DomainWarpCurl, volumetric-3d4d] A finite displacement along a divergence-free field is only volume-preserving to first order; large Amplitude should go through Progressive fractal steps. 4D version costs 6 potentials; a cheaper 'warp xyz only, w passthrough' mode breaks nothing for animation but is not a 4D divergence-free field.
sources: from memory, not consulted: Bridson, Hourihan, Nordenstam 2007 'Curl-Noise for Procedural Fluid Flow'
master.cost_note: SparseVortex 3^d: polys only, no sqrt, no trig, ~.8x Cellular cost = ~3/10/33 ns; R<=1.2 with jitter +-.3 is seam free.
master.variant_notes: Seven proposals agreeing on a Warp()-family node. Implementation options to weigh: analytic Simplex/Perlin potential from one lattice visit (cheapest), 3D bitangent cross of two gradients vs three-potential curl, 4D paired planes vs six-component 2-form, Bridson boundary mask. Only 2D was prototyped.

queue.name: DomainWarpCurl
queue.reason: Divergence-free warp that does not pinch, at 2/3.5/5 ns via analytic Simplex (J1, J4 top pick). SparseVortex potential is the fresh part. Curl mode of domain-warp-source folds in.

domain-warp-flow.look: Stir (angle 90, stir-advect mode): 1 step is just a big curl warp (ring overload); 8-16 Euler steps along the rotated Perlin gradient give genuine ink marbling: long ribbons that fold back on themselves with sharp hooks and spiral eyes, clearly different from the fractal curl and from the existing warps, which never fold a ribbon over itself. L=4 over-stirs into static. RK2 midpoint looks the same with slightly tighter eyes. Watershed (angle 0, descend, flow-watershed mode): with unit-speed steps and no decay every basin fills with concentric ripple rings (fixed-step limit cycle); with step decay 0.7 it converges and gives flat-floored plates with curved borders that are the ridge lines of the potential, not Voronoi: basin value = cobbles / dried mud, basin id = flat-coloured catchment mosaic with a few leftover ripple arcs, source output = fBm gathered into plates. Unnormalised speed overshoots into chaos. Spiral sink (angle 30-60) collapses stripes into plates or wavy curls, not the iconic whorls promised. Path Average gives a streaky LIC-like smear with visible step banding; Min/Max collapse on a hard source. 3D works with Up-axis curl: XZ slice is marbled and the isosurface is a folded ribbon field.
domain-warp-flow.dims: 2D and 3D measured; 4D same loop with d+1 taps, not prototyped
domain-warp-flow.range: [-1,1] follows the source for stir; watershed basin value is the potential at the landing point (measured -0.97..0.53 over seeds), needs ScaleOutput
domain-warp-flow.artifacts: stir filaments alias beyond L ~1.5; watershed ripple arcs where unconverged; path Average step banding; 15-30x Perlin cost
domain-warp-flow.node_shape: DomainWarpFlow: Potential (GeneratorSource), Steps, Length (hybrid), Angle (hybrid; 90 stir, 0 descent), Direction, Normalise, Step Decay, Output {Warp, Travel, Basin Id, Basin Value}, Path Mode {End, Average}; covers stir-advect and flow-watershed
domain-warp-flow.port_notes: Fixed step loop, forward differences, FMA assembly of cos(A) g + sin(A) J g. Stir filaments stretch exponentially with N*L: probe c0ratio 3.3 / slope 602 at L=1 steps 8, 1.0 / slope 2000 at L=1.5-2 steps 12 (continuous by construction, sub-1e-3-feature filaments), so document L <= 1 per feature. Watershed is truly discontinuous at ridges (c0ratio 1.49). Normalise + decaying step required for descent; clamp |h g| per step. Scalar: 6 steps 906 ns, 12 steps 1609 ns (31.8x), watershed 8 steps 1105 ns (22.3x).

critic.params: ang=90,pot=3,U=2.5,zb=.5,sx=.5,pf=1.5,bf=.5,jm=.6,steps=6,L=1.2 (jets) | same with steps=12,sG=6,sc=.25,sd=.8 (Jupiter storms) | ang=90,steps=6,L=2,ax3=1,src=1 (3D marble)
critic.notes: Ship, second to curl and much smaller than proposed: Potential (GeneratorSource), Steps, Amplitude, Mode {Curl, Gradient}, optionally Path Average. Plain stir and plates move to the cheaper analytic curl node, so this one earns its place only where the potential matters. That case is real: a graph potential with zonal jets gives Kelvin-Helmholtz rollups along band edges, and sparse oval discs in the potential give large spirals that the bands wrap around. This is the only real Jupiter in the family because the eddies grow from the flow rather than being stamped on. Six seeds: 555, 90210, 42, 1337 and 2024 show a large spiral, seed 7 only rollups. It holds in a 24 feature window with varied band widths. Remove Normalise and Step Decay: plain descent at a step of 0.19 features or less is at least as clean. Remove Basin Value, since wiring the potential in as Source gives the same thing, and remove Basin Id, which is flat mosaics with splinter fragments. Path Average is the one output I would keep as optional: a fibrous brush-streak look no small graph gives, at Steps source evaluations. I did not compare it with flow-strokes.
critic.improved: Added to t_domain_warp_flow.cpp (additive; previous copy t_domain_warp_flow.prev2.cpp, prototyper original t_domain_warp_flow.prev.cpp): jm bent jets, sG oval storms in the potential, an analytic gradient, ax3 cycled axis. Jets with storms helped a lot and are the best image of the family. Analytic gradient cut scalar cost 35% on the same 6 steps. Cycled axis on fBm gives a marbled XZ slice with one potential per step, z continuity max 0.0963 at L 2 against 0.0900 for up axis at L 1.

tournament.notes: Ship, second to curl and much smaller than proposed: Potential, Steps, Amplitude, Mode, optionally Path Average. Plain stir and plates move to the curl node. It earns its place through graph potentials: jets plus storms are the family's only real Jupiter and its best image, on 5 of 6 seeds and at window 24. Remove Normalise and Decay, since plain descent at step 0.19 is at least as clean. Remove Basin Value, since the potential as Source does the same, and Basin Id, which shows splinter fragments. Path Average gives a fibrous brush look worth keeping as optional, not compared with flow-strokes. Timings reproduced: steps=12 1504 ns (30x perlin2), steps=6 890-991 ns; analytic gradient 647 ns; storms 2526 ns (50x). AVX2 real graphs: 6 steps 33.01 / 66.61 / 104.40 ns, jets 190 nodes 53.15 / 92.72 / 151.44 ns. c0 falls to 1.0-1.3 at strong settings from filaments. Watershed ridges are real jumps and draw comb in relief; at window 24 they read close to warped cellular.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: estimate: Steps x (d+1) potential taps + source: 6 steps on Perlin ~20 / 53 / 130 ns, 12 steps double; watershed 8 steps ~27 / 70 / 170 ns

artist-terrain.note: Jupiter storms on 5 of 6 seeds are the best planet image in the set, but only with a hand-built potential (jets + discs). Plain stir modes are 17.5x Perlin, c0 3.3.

artist-material.note: Jupiter storms is the best fluid image in the set. Costly, and c0 collapses at strong settings. Angle 0 with Path Average could be a slope blur, but nobody rendered that.

voxel-engineer.note: Jupiter is the best single swirl image in the set, on 5 of 6 seeds. 53 ns 3D est at 6 steps, so bake or planet texture, not voxel density.

maintainer.note: Genuine ink marbling and Jupiter storms: ribbons fold over themselves, which no existing warp does. 20-50 ns est and c0 3.3; a second-tier warp with Potential, Steps, Amplitude only.

graphics-researcher.note: Euler advection in a potential is a known idea, but ribbons that fold back on themselves with spiral eyes cannot be made by any existing warp, and the Jupiter jets-plus-storms image holds on 5 of 6 seeds. 15-30x Perlin.

creative.note: Ink with fine filaments, and the Jupiter discovery is a real gas giant.

master.one_liner: Advect the sample point through N steps along the rotated gradient of any potential node: curl gives ink marbling, gradient gives watershed cells, path modes give slope blur and LIC.
master.look:
Look-tested (modes 25, 26). 6 curl steps: vortices, folded ink marbling. A=0 L=1: leathery glossy plate cells, not Voronoi, with basins and curved seams. Slope blur on a hard mask: crumbled, eroded coastlines. Single-step curl alone looked ordinary, so the multi-step is what matters.
[SpiralSinkWarp, dynamics-iteration] Verified in prototype. Dense field of hooks, whorls and spiral arms, one per basin, in both rotation senses around maxima and minima; like Van Gogh swirl, hurricane fields, or ammonite ribs. Hillshade reads as wind-carved scrolls. Good for storms, gas giants, stylised ornament, fur whorls.
master.algorithm: q = p. For i in 0..Steps-1: psi0 = Potential(q); g = forward-difference gradient of Potential at q; v = cos(A)*g + sin(A)*J*g, where J is antisymmetric (2D J(x,y) = (-y,x); 3D J = cross(axis, .); 4D pairs xy and zw). If Normalize: v /= sqrt(|g|^2 + eps). q += v * Length / Steps. If PathMode != End: acc = Combine(acc, Source(q)). Result: PathMode == End ? Source(q) : acc (Average, Min, Max). A = 90 degrees: v is divergence free in every dimension and psi is conserved along the exact flow because g.J.g = 0, so the warp cannot pinch. A = 0: hill climbing; every point falls toward a basin peak of psi, so Source is sampled near the peak, giving a segmentation into catchments with curved organic borders. A = 0 with Average/Min/Max is Substance-style Slope Blur; A = 90 with Average is a line integral convolution.
master.why_new: Existing warps take one evaluation of a built-in noise and pinch. Here the vector field comes from any graph (terrain, cellular, masks) and is iterated. Watershed segmentation in particular is a shape family absent from the sheet. A graph cannot express this because it requires per-lane gradient of a subtree at moved positions, repeatedly.
master.simd_plan: Constant Steps, no per-lane loop exit. Steps*(dim+1) Potential evals + 1 Source (or Steps Source evals in path modes). At 6 steps on Perlin potential: 18/24/30 evals = 20/53/129 ns. J is fixed per node so no branching. Implement as Warp() so the DomainWarpFractal family can wrap it. 4D is a pure function of the torus coordinates, so tiling survives. Justify cost by look; 2D use is affordable, 3D medium, 4D expensive.
master.continuity: C0 for finite steps with a C1 potential and Normalize off: measured c0ratio 6.5 (curl) and 7.6 (A=0). Normalize on makes the field discontinuous at critical points. Path modes on a discontinuous source stay discontinuous.
master.params: Source, Potential (generators), Steps (int), Length (hybrid), Angle (hybrid), Normalize (bool), Path Mode enum, Axis (3D), Gradient Step h.
master.risks:
Euler overshoot at high speed gives fine tangled filaments that alias (maxSlope 241 in the test), so a midpoint option may be needed. Needs a C1 potential; F1 potentials misbehave. A=0 collapses Source detail. Path modes show the discrete step count as bands on hard masks. LIC with gradient-noise input looked weak with visible lattice grid in my test (white-ish input would be needed), so LocalFrame rotate is the better streak tool.
[SpiralSinkWarp, dynamics-iteration] The source needs to be 3..6x higher frequency than the flow or arms do not show. Unit-speed steps cause small limit cycles at the sink centres, visible as a tiny knot; decay the step. In 3D the look is less iconic.
master.cost_note: At 6 steps on Perlin potential: 18/24/30 evals = 20/53/129 ns.
master.variant_notes: Angle sets the regime: 0 is a pure gradient flow, 90 is curl, in between is a spiral sink (SpiralSinkWarp, whorls and hurricane arms, with both senses around maxima and minima).

queue.name: DomainWarpFlow
queue.reason: N-step advection on any potential: marbling and slope blur with high wow, at Steps x (D+1) evals. One test covers stir-advect and flow-watershed as modes.

vortex-cells.look: Exact disc rotations composed over 2 layers. Alone on straight bands (turns 0.5-1) it gives neat comma hooks and at turns 2-4 tight lollipop spirals sitting on bands that stay perfectly straight between discs: a stamped ornament, not a flow, because nothing moves outside a disc and discs are capped at half a cell. With Density 0.25-0.5, wider bands (bf 0.6) and a gentle curl pre-warp (bg 0.3) it becomes discrete oval eyes and teardrop storms on gently waving bands, the closest thing in this family to a cartoon Jupiter, and at turns 2.5 the eyes are closed concentric ovals like the Great Red Spot. The eyes still read as stamped on rather than grown from the band flow. 3D works: spheres rotate about hashed axes, isosurface cut faces show spirals. Spin bias (one-way cyclones) changes little visually.
vortex-cells.dims: 2D and 3D measured; 4D (rotation in a hashed plane) not prototyped
vortex-cells.artifacts: disc outlines at low turns; cores alias at >= 2.5 turns; untouched bands between discs
vortex-cells.node_shape: Exact-rotation kernel of DomainWarpCurl's sparse potential: Turns (hybrid), Radius Min/Max, Density, Spin Bias; layers = chain two nodes
vortex-cells.port_notes: 1x1 window (disc inside its cell), floor recomputed from the moved point per layer. c0ratio 1.76 / slope 1134 at turns 1.5 on a frequency-1 source are sub-1/125-feature spiral arms, not jumps (the map is a continuous bijection); with the pre-warp the probe reads 3.0 / 505. Hard per-disc density gate would pop under a hybrid Density. Scalar timing dominated by harness overhead (139 vs 149 ns for 1 vs 2 layers).

critic.notes: Ship as its own small swirl node, not as a kernel of DomainWarpCurl. An exact disc rotation is not derived from a potential, shares no code with the Perlin loop and has different parameters. The report judged it on bands, where it does read as stamped ovals with straight bands between them. With per-layer lacunarity on fBm it is a different thing: spiral curls at several scales, a stylised cloud or Van Gogh sky, with a clean FFT and fractal curls in the threshold view. The look can be built from existing nodes (curl of a per-cell bump kept inside its cell) and comes out clean, but one scale in regular rows, at 249 nodes and 514.48 / 1482.48 / 4938.93 ns AVX2 for 8 steps. So the case is cost and variety, not impossibility. Its main value over the 2x2 impulse is that site count does not grow with dimension. Stylised work only, hence useful 4.
critic.improved: No code change. Tuned the lac parameter from the earlier critic pass with turns and layers. Clearly the best picture of this idea.

tournament.notes: Ship as its own small swirl node, not a curl kernel. On bands it is stamped ovals, as reported. With per-layer lacunarity on fBm it gives spiral curls at several scales, a stylised cloud look, with a clean FFT. A real graph reaches the look cleanly but at one scale in regular rows, 249 nodes and 514.48 / 1482.48 / 4938.93 ns at 8 steps, so the case is cost and variety, not impossibility. c0 2-3 comes from tight arms. Faint row regularity in the wide view. XZ slice has z-aligned columns because layers rotate only in XY, which the port must fix. Stylised work only.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: estimate: 2-3 ns per layer 2D, 3-4 ns 3D (floor, hash, compare, masked sin/cos)

artist-terrain.note: Stamped ovals on bands; with lacunarity on fBm a stylised multi-scale cloud swirl with clean FFT. Small swirl node, 2-3 ns per layer estimate.

artist-material.note: Multi-scale spiral curls like stylised painted clouds. Distinctive, with some hard edges to watch.

voxel-engineer.note: Stylised swirl stamps; XZ columns in 3D are a fault that needs fixing.

maintainer.note: Stamped ovals with straight bands between; a stylised ornament, not a flow. The lacunarity-on-fBm cloud curls are nice but niche.

graphics-researcher.note: Stamped ovals on bands; multi-layer spiral curls on fBm are a usable stylised cloud. Not a flow.

creative.note: Tiny scroll curls on clouds, Van Gogh ornament. Surprising at this size.

master.one_liner: Exact finite rotation inside hashed discs, in Warp family form: real spiral eddies with zero pinch at about 2 ns per layer.
master.look:
Gas-giant bands with cyclones, ocean eddies, marble curls, Van Gogh swirl, smoke. With strata the prototype instantly reads as Jupiter. Uses: planet textures, water, stylised clouds, wood knots. Prototyped: mode=8.
[WhirlFold, stamp-scatter] Prototype with FBm or stripes behind it: marbled eddies, curls and hooks at a controlled size, like Jupiter bands, Suminagashi ink, or wood-grain knots on a Gradient source. Clearly different from the Warp thumbnails on the sheet, which are ropey and lack discrete vortices.
master.algorithm:
For each layer l: rotate and offset lattice. cell = floor(u). h = hash. R in [.25,.5], c = cell + .5 + (.5-R)*(h2,h3) (inside cell, 1x1 window). d2 = |u-c|^2/R^2. If d2<1: ang = Turns*2*pi*rnd11(h4)*(1-d2)^2, u = c + Rot(ang)*(u-c). Compose sequentially over 2-3 layers with different rotation offsets. Every disc is a shear flow mapped exactly: rigid circles rotate, so area and local isotropy on each circle are preserved and no pinching occurs. Warp returns displacement; can also be an ordinary domain node.

[WhirlFold, stamp-scatter] For rep in Layers, for each colour c in 3^dim: recompute floor(p) from the current, already-moved p (essential), get the unique colour cell g = 3*floor((floor(p)+1-c)/3)+c. Feature f, radius r<=1 (same-colour stamps are 3 cells apart with centres at least 2 apart, so same-colour discs never overlap and each colour is one well-defined global map). t = |p-f|/r, angle a = Amount*rnd11(h)*(1-t^2)^3 for t<1 else 0. Rotate p about f by a: this preserves radius, so it is invertible with exact inverse (run colours in reverse with -a). 3D: rotate about a random unit axis from hash via Rodrigues; 4D: rotate in one or two hash-chosen planes. Warp() returns p_out - p_in. Pinch mode: scale the radial coordinate by a monotonic function of t (stays bijective while dr'/dr > 0).
master.why_new: DomainWarp nodes create smooth folds with stretching, not discrete eyes with many wraps. Summed vortex velocity kernels (see cl_vortex prototype in the lab) only approximate a small-time flow; this form allows many whole turns at no distortion cost.
master.simd_plan:
Per layer: floor, 1 hash, compare, sin+cos: about 2 ns (estimate). 2 layers total about 4 ns in any dim. 3D: rotate about hashed axis with Rodrigues, or about sphere normal for planets. 4D: rotate in a hash-chosen plane or two planes. Fits Warp() interface so it composes into DomainWarpFractal chains.
[WhirlFold, stamp-scatter] Fits the DomainWarp interface. Per colour: floor, one hash, sqrt, polynomial, sin+cos of the angle (or a cheaper rational rotation). 9 or 27 or 81 per layer. Estimate 2D ~10-15 ns per layer, 3D ~40 ns per layer, 4D ~130 ns per layer. Cost is 2-3x CellularDistance and includes no source eval except the warped one downstream; a single-layer lookup avoids the second pass.
master.continuity: C-infinity-ish away from the mask edge and C1 at it because of the cubed falloff. Verified scalar: c0ratio 7.86 at Amount 1.5 and 7.24 at Amount 3 with one layer. At Amount 6 with two layers the reading fell to 1.81, with max slope 584: composed stretching makes extremely steep gradients; I attribute this to compounding because the lower-amount runs are clean and the geometry cannot seam, but I did not separately prove it at that amplitude.
master.params: Cell Size, Turns (hybrid), Layers (int), Radius Min/Max, Spin Bias (signed, for one-way cyclones), Warp Amplitude maps to Turns.
master.risks:
Discs are visibly circular at low Turns. Overlap with another lens's VortexWarp, so choose one or keep both as variants. High Turns with fractal source aliases at the shear ring.
[WhirlFold, stamp-scatter] High amount yields aliasing in the warped source, not a real tear, but it looks like noise at low resolution. Hybrid Amount must stay spatially smooth or lose bijectivity. Since this needs recomputed floors, the proto's first version with a fixed window gave seams; that detail is easy to get wrong. Non-periodic colour pattern is not an issue here because the order is invisible except in overlap.
master.cost_note: Per layer: floor, 1 hash, compare, sin+cos: about 2 ns (estimate). 2 layers total about 4 ns in any dim.
master.variant_notes: Sequentially composed exact rotations, hence a true bijection. Two orderings: one disc inside its own cell per layer (VortexCells, 1x1 window), or colour-ordered 3^d cells with radius up to 1 (WhirlFold). Floors must be recomputed from the moved position or seams appear.

queue.name: VortexCells
queue.reason: Exact disc rotations in a 1x1 window at ~2 ns per layer: Jupiter bands with no pinch. Cheapest of the eddy trio; discs show at low Turns.

scatter-warp.look: Kernel by kernel at matched mean displacement: Vortex produces exactly the same picture as DomainWarpCurl's SparseVortex potential (it is the same kernel), so that kernel is not a second node. Sink/Source pinches bands into lens bulges and on Worley stamps circular dimple rims; with 3 progressive octaves on fBm it gives a bubble-wrap / soap-foam cell look that nothing else in the family makes. Push folds bands into incoherent closed loops. Shear is a weak wobble. Impulse (exact rotation displacement, many radians) at R 0.6 and turns 0.4-0.7 gives clean comma curls and paired spirals in the bands, 2 octaves gives a stirred-paint field of curls at two scales (Van Gogh); because overlapping rotations are summed, not composed, turns >= 1 with overlap makes linked double rings and broken concentric circles. Impulse at low density looks the same as VortexCells with a softer rim. 3D works for all kernels (hashed axis); isosurface shows curled cut faces.
scatter-warp.dims: 2D and 3D measured; 4D needs an orthonormal pair per stamp, not prototyped
scatter-warp.artifacts: impulse overlap rings at >= 1 turn; push kernel incoherent
scatter-warp.node_shape: Kernel enum {Vortex, Sink, Impulse} of DomainWarpCurl's sparse potential; Push and Shear not worth a mode
scatter-warp.port_notes: Per-kernel scale constants (2.33 vortex/sink, 0.96 push, 3.35 shear) make A=1 give mean displacement 0.71 like the reference warps. Scalar vortex 269 ns vs the curl proto's identical kernel at 184 ns: extra rndDir2 and param reads, not maths. Impulse 318 ns.

critic.notes: Keep one thing: the Impulse kernel on a 2x2 window, as an overlap mode of the swirl node. On bands it is the best curl picture in the family, with larger interlocking curls and a fractal threshold view, and it is cleaner than vortex-cells by the probe. The 2x2 window looks as good as 3x3 for less work. Drop the rest. Vortex: concentric rings in calm bands, not spirals; a real warp with a sparse F1 bump as amplitude reaches a weaker, more clustered version at 7 nodes and 8.03 ns. Sink: its foam is the same glass-crumple family as a progressive gradient warp, rounder and less lattice aligned, so Gradient mode of curl covers it closely enough. Push and Shear were not re-rendered by me; the report calls them incoherent and weak. I disagree with merging it into curl: Impulse is a summed rotation, not a potential, and the enum would add a heavier cost class to a cheap node.
critic.improved: Tried win=2, which already existed in the prototype: same look as 3x3 at lower site count. Galleries left as they were.

tournament.notes: Keep only the Impulse kernel on a 2x2 window as an overlap mode. On bands it is the best curl picture in the family: larger interlocking curls, c0 6.38 slope 228, and it looks as good as 3x3. Drop the rest. Vortex gives concentric rings, and a real warp with a sparse F1 bump amplitude reaches a weaker version at 7 nodes and 8.03 ns. Sink is close to a progressive gradient warp. Push and Shear not re-rendered by me. Reported timings reproduced (vortex 270 ns, impulse 304 ns). Site count grows 4 / 8 / 16 with dimension. The 3D slice is spots on flat gray at R 0.6, so 3D needs its own radius or density. Not a curl kernel: Impulse is a summed rotation, not a potential.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: estimate: 3x3 window ~3 / 10 / 33 ns per octave; impulse ~1.5x for sin+cos per site; 2x2 window about half

artist-terrain.note: Impulse kernel on bands gives the best comma curls in eddies; rest duplicates curl or gradient warps. Overlap mode of vortex-cells.

artist-material.note: Big interlocking curls on bands look like a woodblock wave print. Strong but narrow.

voxel-engineer.note: Good curls on bands in 2D, 3D not solved.

maintainer.note: Vortex kernel is identical to DomainWarpCurl SparseVortex; only the 2x2 Impulse kernel has its own picture. Mode at most.

graphics-researcher.note: Impulse curls on a 2x2 window are the best band curls in the family; the rest duplicates.

creative.note: Spirals along bands, a good planetary look.

master.one_liner: A domain warp built from scattered vector stamps (vortices, sources/sinks, directional pushes, shear ribbons) summed over the lattice window, giving discrete eddies and whirlpools instead of smooth noise warps.
master.look:
Swirled bands: gas-giant stripes with embedded storms when the source is horizontal Bands (A about 1.6, Density 0.5). Curly eddies on FBm. Strong amplitude tears into marble. Through DomainWarpFractalProgressive, eddies at multiple scales. Prototype: dcc_lens mode=9.
[ScatterWarp, stamp-scatter] Visible whirlpools, eddies, cyclone bands, fingerprint-like curls, galaxy arms, spiral marbling, and 'stirred paint' when applied to stripes or Checkerboard; sink kernels pinch the texture into dimples, push kernels create slip bands. Current warps (Gradient, Simplex, Fractal) produce smooth, uniform marbling; there is no way today to get localised rotation with a clean eye.
master.algorithm:
Implements the DomainWarp Warp() interface (adds to the positions). For each cell in the 2^d window: centre, h, s, strength a = Amplitude*(1 + Jitter*rnd11(h)), optional sign from a hash bit. d = (p - centre)/s; r2 = dot(d,d); env = (1 - r2)^2 for r2<1 (C1 at the edge).
Kernel enum:
- Vortex: 2D v = a*env*(-d.y, d.x); 3D v = a*env*(axis x d) with axis a random unit vector (or fixed Up); 4D: rotation in a random 2-plane (bivector) represented by two orthonormal random vectors e1,e2: v = a*env*(dot(d,e2)*e1 - dot(d,e1)*e2).
- Source/Sink: v = a*env*d (sign bit chooses).
- Push: v = a*env*u with random unit u (per stamp direction).
- Shear ribbon: v = a*env*u*dot(d, perp(u)) (a local rotation-free shear).
- Dipole: v = a*env*(u - 2 d dot(d,u)) ... (optional).
Sum v over cells, scale by Feature Scale, add to positions. Octaves as in Scatter (coarse eddies plus fine ones = a cheap 'turbulence cascade').
Because vortex and shear fields are divergence free inside the envelope (up to the envelope gradient term), area is nearly preserved: textures swirl rather than stretch.
master.why_new: DomainWarp nodes read a scalar noise's gradient; they cannot produce a rotation centre or a sink. Building a vortex field from existing nodes would need vector output, which only the Warp family has. This reuses the Scatter lattice but emits vectors, so it belongs in the DomainWarp family and chains with DomainWarpFractalProgressive for free.
master.simd_plan: Per cell: hash, centre, envelope (~25 ops), kernel (~10-20 ops), accumulate d components. No source eval, no trig (random unit vectors via normalised rnd11 pairs/triples). 2D 4 cells ~2.5 ns, 3D 8 cells ~7 ns, 4D 16 cells ~20 ns, i.e. in the same band as DomainWarpGradient to Simplex. Dimension agnostic except the kernel's rotation construction.
master.continuity: C1 displacement (t^3 at the boundary), so warped output is as continuous as its source. Measured c0ratio 7.47 on a high-frequency banded source, which is steep rather than broken.
master.params: Kernel enum, Feature Scale, Amplitude (Warp Amplitude, hybrid like the other warps), Size, Size Jitter, Jitter, Strength Jitter, Signed bool (random handedness), Axis enum for 3D (Random/Up), Octaves, Seed Offset.
master.risks:
Large amplitudes fold the domain and create overlaps (true of all warps). 4D plane rotation needs an orthonormal pair per stamp (Gram-Schmidt, ~20 ops). Prior art exists in fluid-like texture synthesis (vortex particles, curl noise), but not as a lattice-window warp node.
[DomainWarpVortex, dcc-tools] At high amplitude the tangent push moves points far outside the rotation arc and folds occur; iterating with less amplitude is better. Far fewer swirl features than cells unless Density is near 1. 3D axis table visible if too small.
master.cost_note: 2D 4 cells ~2.5 ns, 3D 8 cells ~7 ns, 4D 16 cells ~20 ns, i.e. in the same band as DomainWarpGradient to Simplex.
master.variant_notes: Summed tangential or radial kernels, first-order in amplitude. For many-radian swirls see ImpulseWarp and VortexCells.

queue.name: ScatterWarp
queue.reason: 2^d-window vector stamps (vortex, sink, push, shear) in Warp form give local art control. Most general of the eddy trio; try impulse-warp spirals as a kernel.

domain-warp-source.look: With a one-octave Perlin potential the FD curl/gradient/independent modes reproduce DomainWarpCurl's pictures exactly (same potential, 3 taps instead of one analytic lattice visit), so the node adds nothing there. With a multi-octave potential the FD curl is not marbling: because every fBm octave contributes equally to the gradient, the finest octave dominates and the warp becomes fine wrinkling (crumpled-tissue cells at A 0.2, ragged jagged bands at A 0.5). The surprise is a Cellular F1 potential: grad F1 is the unit vector from the nearest site, so gradient mode shears each Voronoi cell radially and curl mode rotates each cell about its site; bands and fBm break into Voronoi shards with tears at the cell edges, a broken-glass / cut-gem facet look that no existing graph can make (saved as a discovery). A Terrace potential warps only in rings along the step contours (quilted ring pattern, more artifact than look). Caution found on the way: FD of the lab simplex2 helper (r2=0.5 kernels) amplified its tiny jumps into grain; FastNoise's Simplex should be checked for the same before it is offered as a potential. 3D (grad phi x grad psi, 8 forward taps) works but the cross product scales as |g|^2 so the 3D amplitude needs to be ~4x smaller than 2D for the same look; isosurface is a lumpy wrinkled field.
domain-warp-source.dims: 2D and 3D measured; 4D gradient/independent dimension agnostic, 4D curl not prototyped
domain-warp-source.artifacts: fBm potentials give wrinkles not swirls; Cellular potential tears by design; 3D amplitude mismatch
domain-warp-source.node_shape: DomainWarpSource: Potential (GeneratorSource), Mode {Gradient, Curl, Independent}, Epsilon, Warp Amplitude hybrid. Worth it for generality (Cellular facet mode, masks, any graph), not for fBm marbling
domain-warp-source.port_notes: Warp() with a GeneratorSource potential. Forward differences (d+1 taps) default; central measured 17% slower scalar with no visible gain. Amplitude is potential dependent (perlin 0.71, 4-oct fBm 2.0, Worley F1 0.83 mean displacement at A=1). Cellular potential tears at cell edges (maxSlope 316, 3D dz jump 0.62). Scalar: perlin fwd 250 ns, central 294 ns, 3-oct fBm 571 ns (11.5x).

critic.notes: This is DomainWarpFlow at Steps=1, same forward differences, so it is a preset, not a node. At one step everything it does is a real graph of DomainOffset, Multiply, Subtract and an offset potential: 12 nodes and 6.19 ns AVX2 on Perlin. I built its showpieces from existing nodes and they hold up. Facet from a Euclidean F1 potential is 12 nodes and 18.12 ns, and looks like the prototype apart from wider breaks in place of thin tears. Fluted cones are 16 nodes and 21.21 ns with the same star pits and fluted relief. Independent fractal warps at comparable strength give rough blobby cells rather than stars, so the look does need curl, but not a new node. The report is right that fBm curl gives jagged wrinkled bands rather than marbling, and that a terrace potential gives contour scratches. Its value is authoring, which a Steps=1 flow node gives for free.
critic.improved: No change to the prototype. Built the real-node graphs above and a per-cell shift (DomainOffset from two CellularValue nodes, 4 nodes, 21.10 ns), which gives straight fault-line shards, a third facet look.

tournament.notes: This is DomainWarpFlow at Steps=1, so a preset, not a node. Everything it does is a real graph at one step: 12 nodes and 6.19 ns on Perlin, facet 12 nodes and 18.12 ns, fluted cones 16 nodes and 21.21 ns, all looking like the prototype. Report is right that fBm curl gives jagged wrinkles rather than marbling and that a terrace potential gives contour scratches. Value is authoring only. Seed 90210: facet c0 6.04, cones c0 7.99. Scalar 252 ns reproduces the reported 250.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: estimate: forward stencil on Perlin ~3.3 / 9 / 22 ns per warp octave; 3D curl 8 taps ~18 ns; fBm potentials multiply by octaves

artist-terrain.note: DomainWarpFlow at Steps=1, all of it a 12-16 node stock graph; the facet-shatter and fluted-cone recipes are worth saving as presets.

artist-material.note: It is flow at Steps=1, and the graph reproduces it. A preset.

voxel-engineer.note: Steps=1 of flow, and a graph at 6.19 ns. Looks poor in thumb and vol.

maintainer.note: DomainWarpFlow at Steps=1; everything it does is a 12-node graph at one step. Frost stars and facet shatter are presets.

graphics-researcher.note: Flow at Steps=1, a preset. Facet shatter (per-Voronoi-cell shear/rotation) and frost-star fluted cones are good presets.

creative.note: Default is dense zigzag noise. The facet-shatter discovery is the only part worth keeping.

plan_node.why_difficulty: Two code paths behind one Warp(). Guidance is on total path length, measured in the notes. Clamps: Steps 1 to 64, Step Decay 0 to 1, connected gradient to +-16.

members.name: Potential
members.note: Unconnected uses the built-in analytic Perlin potential and the number does nothing. Seed is offset by a constant, otherwise a Perlin Source at the same Feature Scale would be conserved along its own curl and not warp at all.

members.name: Steps
members.note: Prototype det J spread 2.13 / 0.59 / 0.19 at 1 / 4 / 12 steps, folded 28.6 / 0 / 0 %. Real node at the same rms displacement, 16 px per feature: det std 1.79 / 0.53 / 0.44, folded 25.3 / 2.0 / 2.1 %. That 2% is under-resolved pixels: at 512 px per feature and 48 steps det mean 1.002, std 0.043, folded 0.00 %.

members.name: Mode
members.note: Curl stirs, Gradient descends to plates.

members.name: Step Decay
members.note: Step lengths are normalised to sum to 1, so this reshapes the path without changing Warp Amplitude. Descent at Warp Amplitude / Steps of 0.21 features is clean without it, as the critic said.

members.name: Path
members.note: Average weights each sample by its step length, Steps source samples, not available through Warp() so a fractal above uses End. Rendered as a slope blur on a hard mask.

plan_node.expected_cost: Measured with fnlab bench, min of 2 runs, AVX2 2D / 3D / 4D, warp alone on a Constant Source. Built in Perlin, Curl: 1 step 1.88 / 5.84 / 7.54, 4 steps 5.22 / 20.38 / 26.45, 12 steps 14.13 / 59.23 / 76.93. Gradient 4 steps 5.26 / 12.11 / 26.52. Connected Perlin, Curl: 4 steps 14.68 / 39.72 / 80.86, 6 steps 21.83 / 59.25 / 121.31. On a Perlin Source at 4 steps: Path End 6.16 / 22.49 / 30.44, Path Average 8.65 / 28.28 / 42.88. Stock warps for scale: DomainWarpGradient 0.95 / 1.80 / 3.51, DomainWarpSimplex 1.64 / 4.36 / 10.61, DomainWarpSuperSimplex 2.14 / 8.14 / 29.27. The 45 node FD graph it replaces was 24.96 / 44.78 / 72.08. The estimates of 6-8 ns 2D at 4 steps and 20 / 53 / 130 ns on 6 Perlin steps held. 3D curl costs 5 ns a step for its two gradient channels against 3 ns for one.
plan_node.dims: 2D, 3D and 4D are real forms. 2D (g_y, -g_x), 4D (g_y, -g_x, g_w, -g_z) on one potential, measured seamless through GenTileable2D. 3D Curl with no Potential is grad phi x grad psi from two channels of one K1 lattice visit, peak speed 4.8 x rms against 2.3 x in 2D, so it tangles sooner. 3D Curl with a Potential is g x axis with the axis cycling Z, X, Y per step, one potential per step and no dependence on seed, net displacement about 0.58 x path at 3 steps.
plan_node.range: Warp: output is the Source's, Path Average is a weighted mean of Source samples. No ScaleOutput. The measured constants are the speed scales instead, 0.7485 / 0.858 / 0.942 and 0.912 for the 3D cross, so Warp Amplitude is the rms path length on Perlin (measured 0.99 to 1.02 over 3 seeds in every dimension), peak 2.3 x in 2D and 4D, 4.8 x in 3D Curl.
notes: Prototype amplitudes map as Warp Amplitude = 0.75 x A x Feature Scale, the prototype rms speed is 0.75 (mean displacement 0.693 against 0.92 here). L in the flow prototype maps to 1.6 x L x Feature Scale. Gradient mode descends at positive amplitude, so A=-3.33 is 2.5 x Feature Scale.

Measured limits, Steps 4 and 12 on Perlin: no jump found up to about 1 x Feature Scale, thin folds get as sharp as jumps from 2 x, feature sets and entry points disagree from 6 x. Connected fBm: about 1 x the finest octave is clean, 5 x fails parity.

DISAGREEMENT: the eddies critic wanted Curl and Flow as separate nodes. Merged because both are the same step loop and differ only in where the gradient comes from. Split if the two paths read badly in the editor.
The Jupiter look comes from the hand-built potential, not the node. It needs a preset, and scalar cost with that potential is 2526 ns per the terrain lens.
Not a mountain terrain warp: fBm relief becomes streaked folds.

master.one_liner: A DomainWarp-family node whose warp vector is the finite-difference gradient or curl of ANY source node (Cellular, Ridged FBm, Terrace, another warp), so curl-noise advection and 'warp by cellular' become one node and compose with DomainWarpFractalProgressive/Independent.
master.look: Curl warp of a Cellular F2-F1 by a Simplex FBm potential (proto sheetB m9) gives incompressible swirls: the cells are bent and stretched into vortex filaments with no pinching or tearing, whereas gradient warps (m9_gradwarp, and the existing Warp Simplex) crumple and fold the texture. Gradient warp by a Cellular F1 potential pushes everything away from cell centres (bubble-wrap domains); gradient warp by Ridged FBm creases the source along the ridges. Through DomainWarpFractalProgressive, N curl-warp iterations approximate fluid advection: marble, smoke, cirrus.
master.algorithm:
Implements the DomainWarp Warp() interface (vector output allowed only in this family). Params: Potential (GeneratorSource), Warp Amplitude (hybrid), Epsilon, Mode enum {Gradient, Curl, Independent}.
Gradient: w_i = (P(pos + e e_i) - P(pos - e e_i)) / (2e); pos += A * w
Curl 2D: w = (dP/dy, -dP/dx) from the same 4 taps (divergence free)
Curl 3D (Bridson): three potentials P_a = P(seed+a) for a in {0,1,2}; w = (dPz/dy - dPy/dz, dPx/dz - dPz/dx, dPy/dx - dPx/dy); each potential needs only 4 of its 6 axis taps -> 12 taps
Independent: w_i = P(seed + i, pos) (one tap per axis, like DomainWarpGradient but with an arbitrary source)
4D: Gradient and Independent are dimension agnostic; Curl 4D is defined via the 4D cross product of three potentials' gradients (expensive, 3 x 8 taps) or falls back to Gradient on w.
Then the normal DomainWarp machinery applies: Warp() is used by the fractal warp nodes for iterated/progressive warps.
master.why_new: Today the warp field can only be the built-in gradient noises; the Warp() vector is never exposed to the graph and no node can produce one from an arbitrary scalar source. Curl (divergence-free) warps are what make advection-like swirls without the folds that gradient warps create, and 'warp by whatever node you like' opens Cellular/Ridged/Terrace/warped potentials with zero new math per potential type.
master.simd_plan: Warp() overloads per dimension inside DispatchClass<DomainWarpSource>: Gradient 2D taps (4/6/8), Curl 4 taps in 2D, 12 in 3D; Independent D taps. Cost = taps x potential: Simplex potential 2D ~5 ns per warp, 3D curl ~26 ns per warp, i.e. 2-4x the existing DomainWarpSimplex, affordable even inside a 3-octave progressive warp. Branch-free; no lattice window of its own.
master.continuity: C0 whenever the potential is C0 (the warp vector is a finite difference) and the warped source is C0. Curl warps are additionally area preserving to first order so they never fold for small amplitudes, which keeps the warped texture's density uniform.
master.params: Potential (node); Warp Amplitude (hybrid, as in the other warps); Epsilon; Mode; Seed Offset per potential for Curl 3D. Inherits the Warp family's behaviour so it slots into DomainWarpFractalProgressive (Octaves, Lacunarity, Gain) for iterate-N warps.
master.risks: Finite-difference warps of a Cellular potential are discontinuous across cell edges only if the potential is (F1 is C0, so fine; CellularValue is not). Epsilon interacts with the potential's frequency; default to 0.01 of a feature. Curl 4D is heavy; a documented fallback is acceptable since tiling (GenTileable2D) only needs the result to depend on w, which the Gradient/Independent modes satisfy.
sources: Bridson, Hourahine, Nordenstam, Curl-Noise for Procedural Fluid Flow, SIGGRAPH 2007 (recalled, not fetched)
master.cost_note: Taps x potential: Simplex potential about 5 ns per warp in 2D, about 26 ns for 3D curl, so 2-4x DomainWarpSimplex.
